390.stepsAria:
- region "How it works, step through the four beats":
  - list:
    - listitem:
      - button "01 Buy": 01 Buy Hold assets that grow. Never sell them, so the gains are never taxed.
    - listitem:
      - button "02 Borrow": 02 Borrow Live on a line of credit secured by the portfolio. The loan grows; so, usually, do the shares.
    - listitem:
      - button "03 Live anywhere": 03 Live anywhere Spend the loan where life costs less. A smaller loan gives the portfolio an easier race to win.
    - listitem:
      - button "04 Die": 04 Die Heirs inherit at a stepped-up basis. The estate repays the loan and keeps the rest.
390.figureAria:
- figure "Gains never taxed. Loan repaid. The rest is theirs. At death, heirs inherit at a stepped-up basis. The estate repays the $5.5M loan from the top; $13.5M passes on.":
  - text: One plan · four beats $2.5M portfolio · 30 years, age 60 to 90
  - img "Illustrative 30-year plan. A $2.5M portfolio grows to $19.0M while a credit line pays the living costs. Moving from St. Louis to Bangkok cuts the yearly draw from $80K to $47K, so the loan ends at $5.5M instead of $9.4M, below the margin-call line, and the odds the plan holds rise from 63% to 93%. At death the gains tax is wiped out by the step-up in basis, the estate repays the loan, and heirs keep $13.5M.": St. Louis 63% $80K/yr Bangkok 93% $47K/yr $5M $10M $15M $20M Age 60 75 90 At 90 · $19.0M Loan repaid $5.5M Heirs $13.5M
  - list "Key":
    - listitem: "Step-up in basis: the gains tax is gone"
    - listitem: What you paid $1.0M
    - listitem: Loan, living in Bangkok
    - listitem: Same life in St. Louis
    - listitem: Margin call at 50%
  - text: Gains never taxed. Loan repaid. The rest is theirs. At death, heirs inherit at a stepped-up basis. The estate repays the $5.5M loan from the top; $13.5M passes on. Illustrative numbers · a typical path, not a forecast
390.visibleSvgAccName: Illustrative 30-year plan. A $2.5M portfolio grows to $19.0M while a credit line pays the living costs. Moving from St. Louis to Bangkok cuts the yearly draw from $80K to $47K, so the loan ends at $5.5M instead of $9.4M, below the margin-call line, and the odds the plan holds rise from 63% to 93%. At death the gains tax is wiped out by the step-up in basis, the estate repays the loan, and heirs keep $13.5M.
